messages:
rachel: Quick RFC follow-up — we found some mismatches between intake metadata and the mini-bench harness. Can we align adapter surface today?

omar: which mismatches? examples please

rachel: example: batcher assumes `max_seq` present in model manifest but some exports only had `context_len`. Failing assert in bench-runner. stack:
```text
AssertionError: missing max_seq
  at bench/runner.py:122
```

kevin: ugh. that's from the legacy exporter. We should map `context_len` -> `max_seq` in adapter to avoid churn. But also consider a `manifest_version` field so we don't silently tolerate breaking changes.

elaine: +1 on schema version. proposal: adapter exposes `ModelDescriptor` with fields {id, versions, seq_limit, kv_shape} and a migration layer. keep bench dependency minimal.

manny: tradeoff: if adapter normalizes aggressively we hide exporter bugs. Maybe emit warnings in telemetry and fail in strict CI mode.

rachel: agree. def want strictness in CI (preflight) and permissive in runtime. Action: add `manifest_version` and `normalize_context` flag. Also extend smoke inputs for golden prompts.

ci-bot: Note — created ticket ML-2312 to track: onboard/bench/compatibility. (labels: onboard, bench, compatibility)

omar: implementation notes: 1) small shim in intake (python) that normalizes keys and records telemetry, 2) bench changes: update `model_info` interface to accept `seq_limit` and deprecate `max_seq` with a warning, 3) add integration test in prebench that runs exporter outputs through shim and fails CI if new keys missing.

elaine: ok. i'll draft a short RFC update with a code sketch showing the `ModelDescriptor` and migration table. timeline: PRs by EOW, canary next week. Anyone opposed?

manny: fine by me. Also suggest adding a cost budget check for heavy benches to avoid accidental large eval runs during onboarding — gate the benches that exceed X tokens.

rachel: good call. add as a gating check in prebench and mark as optional for manual runs. thanks all :thumbsup:
